title: Prepare a governed runtime remediation batch for schema, write authority, and queue readiness

phases.objective: Prepare a no-secret remediation plan and separately operator-confirmed protected execution paths for exact-SHA deployment, runner verification, the sole missing catalog migration, table-scoped write authority, and final readback without performing live changes during pull-request validation.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The remediation batch contract test runs on the exact PR candidate.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Repository-only checks validate exact migration checksums, verification-only applied migrations, protected one-phase execution, direct-table authority profiles, queue decision paths, and prepared-only PR boundaries without connecting to runtime or executing SQL.
steps: Read the runtime database readiness and write-authority contracts.
Validate the sole missing MCP catalog migration checksum and statement count while proving migrations 225 and 1048 are verification-only and cannot be applied.
Validate session continuity, runtime inventory, and observability writer table bindings and exact SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE operations.
Require protected Production environment approval, immutable Production SHA parity, distinct phase-specific confirmations, and an existing capability envelope before governed mutations.
Prove catalog Apply cannot be retried and table grants cannot widen to schema/global authority, grant option, destructive privileges, or an operator principal.
Validate Redis and SQL fallback decision requirements.
Run the contract test and include it in the canonical test manifest.

Keep migration, grant, database, provider, production activation, and GitHub policy effects disabled during pull-request validation; later dispatches each require separate protected-environment approval.
assertions: The remediation plan remains status prepared-only and authority shadow-library-only.
runtime_mutation_allowed, grant_mutation_allowed, migration_apply_allowed, and production_activation_allowed remain false.
The MCP catalog checksum matches the exact repository artifact; already-applied migrations 225 and 1048 can only be dry-run verified.
All three runtime writer profiles use direct-table bindings with SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE only and no grant option, global write, or schema-wide write.
Each privileged runtime operation runs in one explicitly confirmed protected-environment phase against the exact current Production SHA.
Redis is a decision path and SQL fallback is explicitly safe-degradation only.
No migration, grant, SQL/DB mutation, provider mutation, credential read, force-push, Branch Protection/Rulesets Apply, or Production activation occurs.
